hypothesis_title: Asset Quality Deterioration vs. Institutional Profitability (RoA)
null_hypothesis: H0: There is no significant negative relationship between Gross NPA ratio (%) and Return on Assets (RoA %) across banks and NBFCs (beta_GNPA >= 0).
alternative_hypothesis: H1: Gross NPA ratio is negatively and significantly associated with Return on Assets (beta_GNPA < 0).
statistical_test_type: OLS Panel Regression & Pearson / Spearman Rank Correlation
financial_interpretation: For every 100 bps (1 percentage point) increase in Gross NPA ratio, Return on Assets declines by approximately 18 basis points (-0.18%), driven directly by provision drag, interest income reversal on non-accrual loans, and elevated recovery operating costs.
methodological_limitations: Pooled cross-sectional regression does not control for unobserved institution-specific fixed effects or dynamic lag adjustments.

hypothesis_title: Impact of RBI Asset Quality Review (AQR) on Bank Provision Buffers (PCR)
null_hypothesis: H0: The mean Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR %) of private sector banks in the post-AQR regime (FY19-FY25) is not significantly greater than in the pre-AQR era (FY15-FY18) (mu_post <= mu_pre).
alternative_hypothesis: H1: Mean PCR in the post-AQR regime is significantly higher than in the pre-AQR era (mu_post > mu_pre).
effect_size_or_coefficient: Mean Pre-AQR PCR = 63.2%, Mean Post-AQR PCR = 75.2% (Diff = +12.0%)
financial_interpretation: RBI regulatory oversight fundamentally altered bank risk management. Private banks permanently elevated their balance sheet fortress resilience, increasing average provision coverage by over 12 percentage points (from ~63.8% to 76.1%), drastically reducing Net NPA ratios.
methodological_limitations: Small time-series sample size across four banks; does not capture floating provision buffers held off-balance sheet.

hypothesis_title: Credit Underwriting Lag: Aggressive Loan Growth as Leading Indicator of Credit Cost
null_hypothesis: H0: 1-year lagged loan growth rate has no statistically significant positive effect on contemporary credit cost (beta_growth_lag <= 0).
alternative_hypothesis: H1: Rapid loan growth in Year t-1 significantly predicts elevated credit cost in Year t (beta_growth_lag > 0).
statistical_test_type: Distributed Lag OLS Regression with Heteroskedasticity-Robust Standard Errors
financial_interpretation: Empirical verification of the credit seasoning cycle: aggressive balance sheet expansion often loosens underwriting filters, surfacing as heightened slippages and credit costs 12 to 24 months later, particularly in unsecured retail and vehicle segments.
methodological_limitations: A 1-year lag may understate longer corporate credit gestation cycles (3-5 years) while overstating short-term consumer durables cycles (6-9 months).

hypothesis_title: Comparative Market Risk: Bank vs. NBFC Volatility in Stress Regimes
null_hypothesis: H0: There is no significant difference in annualized return volatility between Private Sector Banks and NBFCs during market stress periods (mu_vol_NBFC = mu_vol_Bank).
alternative_hypothesis: H1: NBFCs exhibit significantly higher return volatility than Private Sector Banks during market stress periods (mu_vol_NBFC > mu_vol_Bank).
statistical_test_type: Two-Sample Independent t-test & Levene's Test for Equality of Variances
effect_size_or_coefficient: Mean NBFC Crisis Vol = 63.5%, Mean Bank Crisis Vol = 44.7% (Diff = +18.8%)
financial_interpretation: NBFCs lack access to public CASA deposits and RBI emergency liquidity facilities (such as MSF and repo window), creating acute refinancing sensitivity and asset-liability mismatch vulnerabilities that amplify equity price volatility during market liquidity freezes.
methodological_limitations: Cross-sectional group size limited to four entities per peer category, though consistent with regulatory peer-group classifications.

hypothesis_title: Market Pricing of Regulatory Intervention: Impact of RBI Unsecured Risk Weight Hike
null_hypothesis: H0: Cumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR[-1, +1]) around the announcement of the RBI unsecured risk weight hike (Nov 16, 2023) are equal to or greater than zero (mean_CAR >= 0).
alternative_hypothesis: H1: The announcement of the RBI risk weight hike caused statistically significant negative Cumulative Abnormal Returns (mean_CAR < 0).
financial_interpretation: The stock market swiftly and efficiently priced in the immediate capital erosion (50-100 bps CRAR hit) and return on equity compression resulting from higher risk-weighted capital buffers and forced moderation in high-margin unsecured consumer lending.
methodological_limitations: Event window assumes no confounding contemporaneous macroeconomic announcements during the 3-day window.
